articles.title: Webb reveals stunning panorama of star formation
articles.description: This starry view of the nearby star-forming region IC 348 is one of the largest images from the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope released to the public so far. Using Webb, astronomers searched IC 348 for brown dwarfs, which are less massive than the smallest stars. The researchers discovered brown dwarfs just twice the mass of Jupiter, bringing the study of these curious objects into a new mass range.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope reveals a breathtaking panoramic view of star formation in IC 348, offering unprecedented insights into how stars are born in nearby regions.

articles.title: BepiColombo begins Mercury arrival with MTM separation success
articles.description: On 3 September 2026 at 15:49 CEST, the European Space Agency's BepiColombo Mission Control Team at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) received the signal they had been waiting for – BepiColombo’s Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) successfully separated from the spacecraft stack. This landmark achievement for the ESA and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) mission marks the first step of BepiColombo's long-awaited arrival at Mercury.
articles.summary: BepiColombo successfully completes its Mercury Transit Module separation on September 3, 2026, marking a landmark milestone in humanity's mission to explore Mercury.

articles.title: BepiColombo’s Mercury arrival begins - full replay
articles.description:
Video: 
			02:31:10
				
Watch the replay of the livestream originally broadcast on 3 September as ESA/JAXA's BepiColombo mission took the first critical step towards arriving at Mercury.
After travelling through the inner Solar System together for eight years, BepiColombo's Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) will separate from the rest of the stacked spacecraft on 3 September 2026. This marks the beginning of one of the most complex planetary arrival sequences ever attempted by ESA.
Broadcast live from ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, the programme includes live views from the iconic Main Control Room, expert analysis, behind-the-scenes insights, and the first signal from the spacecraft following separation. 
Livestream schedule (CEST): 

13:45 – Livestream begins 
16:00-16:45 – End of livestream
articles.summary: The ESA and JAXA celebrate BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury with a complete livestream replay, marking a triumphant moment in international space exploration.

articles.title: NASA just powered up Roman’s massive 300-megapixel camera
articles.description: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope has successfully activated its 300-megapixel infrared camera, which will capture enormous stretches of the cosmos with Hubble-like sharpness. Its planet-hunting coronagraph is also working as expected, putting Roman another major step closer to beginning science operations in 2027.
articles.summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope has successfully activated its revolutionary 300-megapixel infrared camera, marking a major milestone for this transformative mission. This powerful instrument will capture unprecedented cosmic imagery and enable groundbreaking discoveries.

articles.title: The Universe Is Full of Tiny Red Dots—and They’re One of Astronomy’s Biggest Discoveries in Decades
articles.description: A new type of object found in the early universe has puzzled astronomers for years, but they may finally have some answers.
articles.summary: Astronomers may have finally identified the mysterious 'tiny red dots' observed in the early universe by the James Webb Space Telescope. This breakthrough discovery could fundamentally reshape our understanding of early galaxy formation.

articles.title: Astronomers Confirm Youngest Known Planet, Less Than 1 Million Years Old
articles.description: Astronomers have confirmed the youngest known planet yet, a Jupiter-size world less than 1 million years old that orbits a star about 450 light-years from Earth, according to a study published Sept. 16 in The Astrophysical Journal Letters. The planet, designa…
articles.summary: Astronomers have confirmed the youngest known planet ever discovered, a Jupiter-sized world less than 1 million years old. This discovery provides unprecedented insights into planetary formation in real-time.

articles.title: NASA Tests Dual Mode Propulsion CubeSat Ahead of Launch
articles.description: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that paradigm. Engineers at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, recently completed a rigorous series of environmental and physical tests on a new small satellite designed to make spaceflight safer […]
articles.summary: NASA successfully tests an innovative dual-mode propulsion CubeSat that combines volatile fuel and maneuvering systems into a single compact unit, advancing small satellite technology.

articles.title: Hubble Spots Chaotic Secret in Galaxy
articles.description: A chaotic secret hides within this seemingly serene image of spiral galaxy NGC 4698 taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and released on Sept. 18, 2026. As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disk of stars, gas, and dust. These arms […]
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope reveals hidden dynamics within spiral galaxy NGC 4698, uncovering chaotic structures that challenge our understanding of galactic evolution.

articles.title: A galaxy spinning out of sync
articles.description:
Image:
			
Though the spiral galaxy in this new image by the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope seems serene, it hides a chaotic secret. This galaxy is NGC 4698, and it lies about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. It’s one of over one thousand galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, the nearest large cluster of galaxies bound together by gravity.
As a spiral galaxy similar to our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disc of stars, gas and dust. Its centre is dominated by a galactic bulge.
The diffuse off-white glow of the galaxy’s bulge comes from stars smaller, older, and cooler than the massive blue stars that dot the galaxy’s outer disc. These tightly packed stars orbit a supermassive black hole containing millions of times the Sun’s mass. Scientists have found signs that this black hole is actively growing, drawing gas inward with its gravitational pull.
With a flat, starry disc and diffusely glowing centre, NGC 4698 looks a lot like a typical spiral galaxy — but this galaxy is far from normal. NGC 4698 is one of only a few known spiral galaxies with a bulge that extends out from the disc at a right angle. The elongation is faintly visible in this Hubble image, which shows the ghostly glow of the starry bulge peeking above and below the dusty disc. What’s more, the stars and gas nearest the galaxy’s centre rotate perpendicular to the rest of the disc.
What could cause a galaxy to be so out of sync? Astronomers have found that the culprit likely lies outside the galaxy. If NGC 4698 funneled in gas from an outside source, the newly collected gas could have formed a disc of gas and stars in the galaxy’s centre, at an angle relative to the rest of the disc. Some observations suggest that this galaxy once experienced a minor galactic merger, as evidenced by a short ‘tail’ of hydrogen streaming from one side of the galaxy.
The data used to create this image come from an observing programme (#18103; PI: Thilker) focusing on galaxies in the Virgo Cluster.
[Image Description: A spiral galaxy viewed at an angle, with a bright central bulge and winding spiral arms. The arms form a ring around the galaxy, without appearing to reach its centre. Prominent red-brown dust lanes weave through the arms, which are also dotted with bright blue and reddish regions of star formation. The galaxy is set against a dark background scattered with stars and faint distant galaxies.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope reveals unexpected rotational dynamics in a spiral galaxy, exposing fascinating chaotic structures that expand our knowledge of galactic behavior.

articles.title: Hubble's superbubble scene
articles.description:
Image:
			
This sprawling cosmic vista and subject of today’s ESA/Hubble Picture of the Month comes from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). The LMC is the largest of the small galaxies that orbit our Milky Way galaxy. At just 160 000 light-years away, the LMC offers a close look at highly active stellar birthsites like the nebula shown here. This nebula is named LHA 120-N44, or N44 for short, and it’s located in the constellation Dorado.
The appearance of this photogenic nebula is dominated by two features: a vast central void and a shell of dense, dusty gas. The central void is a ‘superbubble’ spanning roughly 210 by 140 light-years. The glittering stars at the centre of the void are responsible for its creation; through their powerful stellar winds and explosive supernovae, these stars have expelled much of the gas from which they were born.
When the stars of N44’s central star cluster swept away this gas, the expelled gas formed a shell around the superbubble. New stars are forming in this compressed gas shell, making N44 an interesting target for researchers studying the process of star formation. In particular, astronomers have turned to this nebula as an ideal place to time this process from start to finish. Their goal is to understand how long it takes from the collapse of cold gas clouds into dense knots to the moment nuclear fusion ignites in the heart of a newborn star.
Researchers used Hubble to survey N44 and take a census of its stars, cataloguing nearly half a million stars within the cluster as well as interlopers drifting in front of it. Of the stars surveyed, nearly 30 000 are what astronomers call pre-main-sequence stars, which have yet to begin fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores. This treasure trove of baby stars was discoverable thanks to the high sensitivity and fine spatial resolution of Hubble’s instruments that can pick out faint objects in crowded clusters.
The gas shell surrounding the superbubble is energised by ultraviolet radiation from massive stars, causing it to glow and highlighting several distinct features. Each feature within the broader N44 star-forming complex was catalogued by astronomer Karl Henize in the 1950s. One feature is a smaller bubble, catalogued as N44F, that is located near the upper-right corner of this image. N44F is an interstellar bubble blown by the intense stellar winds of a single hot and massive star. As this previously released Hubble closeup shows, the star’s furious winds and radiation have sculpted the surrounding bubble and created pillars of dusty gas.
The data used to create this image come from an observing programme (#14689; PI: Gouliermis) that aimed to probe stars in the N44 complex that have not yet begun fusing hydrogen into heavier elements in their cores. These data help to determine how long the process of star formation takes, as well as what masses newborn stars typically have. Hubble's sensitive observations of the lowest-mass stars in this region open a new window onto star formation in regions that, like the LMC or the galaxies of the early Universe, are poor in elements heavier than helium.
[Image Description: A dense field of stars fills the image, surrounded by wispy clouds of gas and dust. Pale blue and grey nebulosity forms an intricate web across the scene, with darker clouds of dust concentrated towards the lower right. Numerous bright stars appear in shades of blue, white and orange.]
articles.summary: Hubble Space Telescope captures a spectacular cosmic vista featuring a superbubble structure in the Large Magellanic Cloud, showcasing the dramatic physics of stellar phenomena.

articles.title: Astronomers Find a Sub-Neptune Orbiting Completely Backward Around a Red Dwarf
articles.description: In our own solar system, all eight planets orbit our Sun in a nice, orderly fashion. None are more than 7° or so out of alignment with the equator, and all of them rotate in the same direction as the Sun itself. But that’s not the case for all solar systems, and a new paper published in Astronomy & Astrophysics from a team of researchers led by Yann Carteret, a PhD student at the University of Geneva (UNIGE), describes the first time we’ve ever found an exoplanet orbiting the opposite direction of its red dwarf parent star - and it has major implications for our understanding of planet formation theory.
articles.summary: Astronomers discover a sub-Neptune exoplanet orbiting a red dwarf in a retrograde motion, defying the orderly orbital patterns seen in our solar system and revealing diverse planetary system architectures.

articles.title: Perseverance Reveals How Complex Water Systems Shaped the Jezero Crater on Early Mars
articles.description: A new study reveals that Jezero Crater’s enigmatic ‘Margin Unit’ was shaped by a complex sequence of ancient lakes, groundwater systems, and hydrothermal fluids.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover uncovers evidence that Jezero Crater hosted complex ancient water systems including interconnected lakes and groundwater, advancing understanding of Mars' habitable past.

articles.title: Strange Galaxies in the Early Universe Were Shaped by Weird Stars
articles.description: Galaxies and their stars in the early Universe look a lot weirder than those we see today, and astronomers want to know why. A team of researchers at the University of Utah decided to survey certain stars in nearby galaxies as analogs of those that existed when the Universe was still in its infancy. The survey, called the "Treasury of Extremely Metal-Poor O Stars (TEMPOS), used the ultraviolet (UV) light streaming from those relatively close-by stars as detected by the Hubble Space Telescope's Cosmic Origins Spectrograph.
articles.summary: Astronomers discover that galaxies and stars in the early universe possessed unusual characteristics shaped by exotic stellar populations, providing insights into cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Great news from Saturn's moon Enceladus in the search for life in space
articles.description: What are the chances of finding extraterrestrial life in our solar system? Frank Postberg, a professor of planetary science at Freie Universität Berlin, has published a study in Science Advances with an international team of researchers. They present new evidence that it is easier to determine the constituents of the ocean hidden beneath Enceladus's icy surface than previously assumed.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New discoveries about Saturn's moon Enceladus strengthen the case for subsurface conditions favorable to extraterrestrial life, offering hope in the search for life beyond Earth.

articles.title: Webb detects ammonia and unexpected chill on a distant giant planet
articles.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a team of astronomers led by the University of Maryland identified water, methane and ammonia in the atmosphere of HATS-6 b, a giant planet 500 light-years from Earth. The observations also revealed that HATS-6 b may be significantly cooler than standard calculations predict—suggesting that the planet's relationship with its star may be far more complicated than previously thought.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope detects ammonia, water, and surprisingly cool temperatures on a distant giant exoplanet, expanding our understanding of atmospheric composition in alien worlds.

articles.title: Coolest lava world yet with signs of an atmosphere offers clues to early Earth
articles.description: In the search for extraterrestrial life, it makes sense to first look for rocky planets with an atmosphere, like Earth. Without an atmosphere, a planet can't have surface water. But of the more than 6,300 exoplanets cataloged thus far, the vast majority are not rocky, and only a handful of the rocky worlds appear to have an atmosphere.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered an unusually cool lava world with atmospheric signatures that provides insights into early planetary formation and the conditions necessary for life. This discovery advances our understanding of rocky exoplanets and their potential habitability.

articles.title: “We found something never seen before” – A dead star is producing a shock wave that shouldn’t exist
articles.description: A dead white dwarf with no detectable disk has somehow produced a powerful shock wave that appears to have persisted for at least 1,000 years. Its magnetic field may be partly responsible, but astronomers say an unexplained “mystery engine” may also be at work.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a white dwarf producing a powerful shock wave despite having no detectable disk, revealing an unprecedented stellar phenomenon. This discovery challenges existing models of stellar behavior and opens new avenues for astrophysical research.

articles.title: Ancient meteorites reveal a powerful force that helped build the Solar System
articles.description: Ancient grains inside one of the oldest known meteorites reveal that a surprisingly strong magnetic field existed during the solar system’s first 200,000 years. The discovery suggests magnetism worked alongside gravity to help transform a vast cloud of gas and dust into the sun and planetary disk.
articles.summary: Ancient meteorite grains reveal that a surprisingly powerful magnetic field existed during the early Solar System's formation. This discovery provides crucial insights into the forces that shaped our planetary system billions of years ago.

articles.title: These massive stars could explain Webb’s strangest galaxies
articles.description: Hubble observations of massive stars in metal-poor dwarf galaxies are revealing clues to why the early universe looks so unusual. Researchers found that stellar winds weaken sharply at extremely low metallicities, potentially allowing massive stars to retain more material and evolve in unexpected ways. The team also found large differences in iron abundance, a key ingredient in stellar winds and supernovae.
articles.summary: Hubble observations of massive stars in metal-poor dwarf galaxies are providing explanations for unusual galaxies discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope. This research bridges observations across telescopes to solve cosmic mysteries.

articles.title: First stellar stream beyond the Milky Way could reveal dark matter
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way, opening a new way to study dark matter in distant galaxies. These faint trails of stars trace a galaxy’s gravitational structure and could eventually help scientists map invisible matter across the universe.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way, providing a revolutionary new method to study dark matter. This landmark finding opens unprecedented opportunities for understanding the universe's invisible matter.

articles.title: What Is Humanity’s Place in the Cosmos?
articles.description: A lifelong fascination with terra incognita led the astrophysicist Priyamvada Natarajan to map out the universe’s most enigmatic phenomena.
articles.summary: Astrophysicist Priyamvada Natarajan explores humanity's place in the cosmos through mapping the universe's structure and mysteries. A wonder-driven investigation into our cosmic context and significance.

articles.title: SpaceX Preps For 'Milestone' Starship Flight 14; NASA Updates ISS Mission Timing
articles.description:
SpaceX has completed its rehearsal, started preparing the launch tower for Starship flight 14 next week. NASA eyes ISS mission date.
The post SpaceX Preps For 'Milestone' Starship Flight 14; NASA Updates ISS Mission Timing appeared first on Investor's Busines…
articles.summary: SpaceX prepares for milestone Starship Flight 14 with launch tower rehearsal complete, while NASA updates ISS mission timing. Major progress toward fully operational orbital spaceflight.

articles.description: "Danger" Will Robinson-Smith at Spaceflight Now! SpaceX is on the cusp of sending its massive Starship rocket to orbit for the first time in program history. The Starship Flight 14 mission will carry 26 Starlink Version 3 satellites into low Earth orbit, but …
articles.summary: SpaceX approaches its first orbital flight of the massive Starship rocket. A landmark moment in commercial spaceflight development and reusable launch vehicle technology.

articles.title: Starship 14 : SpaceX tente lundi l’étape qui doit transformer son immense fusée en véritable véhicule spatial
articles.description: Après 13 vols d’essai, SpaceX s’apprête à soumettre Starship à une séquence bien plus exigeante que tout ce qu’il a tenté jusqu’ici. De l’ascension aux dernières manœuvres prévues plusieurs heures plus tard, plusieurs étapes critiques devront réussir pour que…
articles.summary: After 13 test flights, SpaceX prepares Starship for a significantly more demanding flight sequence to transform it into a fully operational space vehicle. A pivotal step toward operational spaceflight.

articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 September 26 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Mirrored Meteor and […]
articles.summary: A stunning APOD image captures the intersection of a meteor and the Milky Way, showcasing the dynamic beauty of Earth's night sky and our galactic home.

articles.title: NASA, Boeing to Provide Update on Starliner Development
articles.description: During a news conference at 3 p.m. EDT on Monday, Sept. 28, NASA and Boeing leadership will discuss Starliner’s development and plans for regular crew flights to and from the International Space Station. Learn where to watch online: https://www.nasa.gov/live The briefing participants include: Media already credentialed for Crew-13 may participate in person at NASA’s Kennedy […]
articles.summary: NASA and Boeing leadership will provide an update on the Starliner spacecraft development, advancing human spaceflight capabilities for crew transport missions.

articles.title: Win a trip to ESA to witness BepiColombo arrive at Mercury
articles.description:
Get ready to celebrate BepiColombo’s arrival at Mercury. Craft a welcoming message that could be a drawing, song, poem or any other art form and stand a chance to win a trip to mission control! 
ENTRY FORM  
Full rules and how to enter below.
articles.summary: The ESA invites the public to celebrate BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury by submitting creative welcome messages, making space exploration a global collaborative experience.

articles.title: Juice to fly past Earth for third gravity assist
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) will return to Earth on 28 September, with flight controllers guiding the spacecraft close to our home planet to alter its speed and direction en route to Jupiter.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) executes its third Earth gravity assist on September 28, advancing toward its groundbreaking mission to Jupiter's moons.

articles.title: Purple swirls on the Red Planet
articles.description: This image shows a prominent ice cliff near Mars’s south pole. With striking swirls of purple, pink and red, it’s a far cry from the colour palette we usually associate with the Red Planet.
articles.summary: Striking purple, pink, and red ice cliffs at Mars's south pole showcase the stunning geological diversity and beauty of the Red Planet.

articles.title: Swiss Engineers Just Designed a Better 'Shock Absorber' for Spacecraft
articles.description: Rocket launches are some of the most violent travel methods man has ever created. They generate millions of pounds of thrust and convert that into intense g-forces. Humans must undergo serious training to withstand those experiences, but machines have to do so as well, but by design rather than training. If a delicate mirror or solder joint cracks before a multi-billion dollar satellite even begins its mission, the years of effort that went into its design and assembly could be lost. Now, researchers in Switzerland have come up with an ingenious way to make sure that is much less likely to happen.
articles.summary: Swiss engineers design an innovative shock absorber system that reduces the extreme vibrations and forces experienced during rocket launches, enhancing spacecraft safety and payload protection.
